correctness.rationale: Global attraction proved by positivity, logistic bounds and backward reciprocal induction. Linear response is exact nilpotent exponential. The maximizing logarithmic ratio gives an iff threshold and positive-time tangency; strict gap from instantaneous reactivity is controlled by compact time intervals. Stirling-Laplace estimates establish both halves of the \(1/4\) logarithmic coefficient; all n and parameter boundaries are explicit. The finite checker corroborates nine n and the n=2 stationary root, without claiming infinite certification.

evidence: Mari et al. (2017), https://doi.org/10.1111/2041-210X.12805, gives a generalized initial-time reactivity test for chosen outputs, not a supremum over later times for fixed initial input.
Yang et al. (2023), https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-023-42580-0, treats large-community reactivity and numerical ecology, not the homogeneous directed all-n onset law.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Classical reactivity is the positive top eigenvalue of the symmetric Jacobian and is genuinely weaker than the positive single-site all-time gain criterion here: a nonempty interval between the two is proved. Weighted-metric theory and generic reactivity bounds do not contain the new coefficient 1/4 or fixed-column global maximization.

value.rationale: Restricted positive one-site pulse is a natural ecological intervention distinct from signed isotropic instantaneous reactivity; a provably nonempty mismatch interval and universal \((\log n)/(4n)\) versus \(n^{-2}\) threshold scaling have interpretable effects at every chain length. The quantity is not a routine restatement of Hurwitz stability or a marginal numerical improvement.
